summary: Backend-only sweep of WatchNexus v1.0.0 RTP (50 controllers). Verified the FFmpeg tier-lock fix end-to-end, auth flow, full tier-gating semantics (Standard 403 -> Ultra 200 -> Deactivate 403), invalid-license rejection, honest-501 stubs, and primary GET endpoints across every listed controller. 73 of 74 pytest tests passed. Only 1 hard failure: GET /api/fortress/status crashes with AmbiguousMatchException -> HTTP 500 due to duplicate route registration (controller + Minimal API).

critical.issue: HTTP 500 — AmbiguousMatchException. The same path is mapped twice: (1) FortressController.Status() at src/watchnexus/core/Controllers/FortressController.cs:212 (`[Route("api/fortress")] [HttpGet("status")]`) AND (2) Minimal API in src/watchnexus/core/Fortress.cs:70 (`app.MapGet("/api/fortress/status", ...)`). ASP.NET cannot select between the two and returns 500 on every call. Reproduces 100% on both Standard and Ultra tiers. Fix: delete one of the two registrations (recommend keeping the controller, removing the Minimal API duplicate). Likely also affects /api/fortress/verify (controller `[HttpPost("verify")]` at line 254 vs `app.MapPost("/api/fortress/verify", ...)` at Fortress.cs:89) and /api/fortress/audit if a controller version exists.

minor.issue: Bug fix only verified after manually installing ffmpeg in the test container (`apt install -y ffmpeg`). The original problem statement claimed ffmpeg was pre-installed at /bin/ffmpeg; it was NOT. Before install: endpoint correctly returned 200 with ffmpeg_installed=false + install_hint='sudo apt install ffmpeg'. After install: 200 with ffmpeg_installed=true, ffprobe_installed=true, path=/bin/ffmpeg, version='ffmpeg 5.1.9-0+deb12u1'. The tier-lock fix itself is confirmed (no 403).

action_items: FIX HIGH: Remove duplicate /api/fortress/status mapping. Delete either the Minimal API block (Fortress.cs lines 70-138) OR the controller method (FortressController.cs lines 212-245). Same likely needed for /api/fortress/verify and /api/fortress/audit*.

Note for prod: bundle or document ffmpeg as a hard prerequisite. The install-hint UX is correct, but the OOBE wizard should NOT proceed past 'ffmpeg detected' if absent (currently it returns 200 even with ffmpeg_installed=false — the frontend gate should block).
Main agent reminder: restore LICENSE_SERVER_URL in /app/src/watchnexus/core/appsettings.json before shipping (offline-only validation was a test scaffold).
critical_code_review_comments: DUPLICATE ROUTE REGISTRATION: Fortress.cs uses Minimal API style (app.MapGet/MapPost) for endpoints that ALSO exist as MVC controller actions. ASP.NET registers both -> 500. Pick one style per resource and standardize.

FortressFilter exempt list (FortressController.cs:52) is a hardcoded single-entry HashSet. As more system-diagnostic endpoints get added (license probes, health checks, update probes) they will repeat the OOBE bug. Suggest a marker attribute like [FortressExempt] on actions instead of a path list.

ProtectedRoutes dict (FortressController.cs:27-42) hardcodes 30+ module codenames inline. Drift risk: new controllers added without tier-map entry will silently be free. Recommend deriving from a single SSOT (e.g. ModuleCatalogue.cs).
test_credentials: owner@watchnexus.local / password123 (Standard); Ultra serial WNX-ULT-AAAA-BBBB-CCCC (offline mode)
seed_data_creation: Installed ffmpeg/ffprobe (apt) on the test container so the ffmpeg detection endpoint could be validated in the positive case. No DB changes.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Test file /app/backend/tests/test_watchnexus_v100_controller_sweep.py is idempotent: it leaves the system on Standard tier (TestZCleanup::test_deactivate_final). Activation logic now checks current tier first so re-runs don't 400. The ONLY failing test is fortress-status — once the duplicate route is removed the whole suite should be 74/74. Per-controller sweep covers 53 endpoints across 50+ controllers; if new controllers are added, append to CONTROLLER_GETS list.

rca of the issue.ffmpeg_fix_verified: PASS. The tier-lock fix (FortressFilter.ExemptPaths containing '/api/crucible/ffmpeg-status') works exactly as designed: the endpoint returns 200 on Standard tier instead of 403 FORTRESS_TIER_LOCKED. After installing ffmpeg in the env, payload correctly shows ffmpeg_installed=true, ffprobe_installed=true, ffmpeg_version, and ffmpeg_path. Cross-platform FfmpegLocator finds the binary via PATH (/bin/ffmpeg).

fortress_status_500.reproduction: GET https://ffmpeg-wizard-2.preview.emergentagent.com/api/fortress/status with a valid Bearer token returns HTTP 500. Tier irrelevant (fails on Standard and Ultra).
fortress_status_500.root_cause: Two route registrations resolve to the same HTTP method + path: (a) [Route("api/fortress")] [HttpGet("status")] in FortressController.cs and (b) app.MapGet("/api/fortress/status", ...) in Fortress.cs (called from Program.cs.MapControllers neighborhood).
fortress_status_500.fix: Delete the Minimal API duplicates in Fortress.cs (lines 70-138) OR delete the controller actions. Controller version is richer (queries Settings table for sealed_at) — recommend keeping controller and dropping the Minimal API block.

rca of the issue.tier_gating_per_controller_table: All controllers exercised on Ultra returned non-500 except fortress-status (above). Pro-locked endpoints correctly returned 403 FORTRESS_TIER_LOCKED on Standard, then 200/empty after WNX-ULT-AAAA-BBBB-CCCC activation, then 403 again after /api/cellar/deactivate. Honest-501 confirmed for POST /api/sprout/feeds, POST /api/gelatin/tunnel/create, POST /api/quality-profiles.
